clue.text: Fan appears less enthusiastic

definitions.meaning: an electric fan is a device that cools a room
comparative of cool in the sense of lukewarm or unwelcoming

explanation.surface: A supporter is showing less zeal than before.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan lowers temperature, so it is a cooling device; cool also means unenthusiastic, and this is its comparative form.

clue.text: Very steady backer invested in musical

indicators.note: invested in means put inside, as money is put into a show

parts.note: Chess is a stage musical by Tim Rice with Benny and Bjorn of Abba
an angel is a financial backer of a theatrical show

explanation.surface: A dependable financier has put money into a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1980s musical by Tim Rice and the Abba songwriters is the container; in theatre slang an angel is a show's financial backer. 'invested' fits the money surface but here signals insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that never alters is constant, completely steady.

clue.text: Animal or bird with no tail

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: with no tail means the final letter of the bird is cut off

parts.note: an ibis is a wading bird with a curved bill

explanation.surface: Asks whether it is a beast or a bird missing its tail feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: IBIS loses its last letter to give IBI.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a small African antelope, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Leader of criminals, given time, finally put behind bars

indicators.note: put means the other letters are placed inside the word for finally

parts.note: end means finally, at the end

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of criminals

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: The gang boss, after a long sentence, is at last locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put behind bars' reads as the definition, but 'put' is needed as the insertion signal, leaving 'behind bars' to define.
explanation.definitionFit: Being shut in a cage is being imprisoned, just as a convict is behind bars.

clue.text: Unlikely description of Thomas

definitions.meaning: the apostle Thomas would not believe in the Resurrection until he saw the wounds, hence 'doubting Thomas'

explanation.surface: A remark that Thomas is hardly the sort to do something.
explanation.definitionFit: Something improbable is open to question; the apostle known for refusing to believe without proof is famously described as doubting.

clue.text: Built-up Italian area south of very large town near Rome

indicators.note: in a down clue, south of means placed below the earlier piece

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing size meaning very large

indicators.note: in a down clue, built up means the letters are written upwards, in reverse

parts.note: It is an abbreviation for Italian, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: A developed district of Italy lies below a big town close to the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Built-up' reverses IT to TI, and 'south of' puts TI and A below OS in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: It was the ancient port of Rome at the Tiber mouth, now a resort district close to the capital.

clue.text: Bungalow undergoing demolition yielded a weapon

indicators.note: a bungalow being demolished is broken apart, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Knocking down a single-storey house turned up a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undergoing demolition' rearranges BUNGALOW into the answer plus the A that the clue says it 'yielded'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a tube through which darts are blown, a hunting weapon.

clue.text: Investor, one with special interest involving business centre

indicators.note: involving means taking the other letters inside

parts.note: a fancier is an enthusiast for one thing, like a pigeon fancier

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle two letters, here of business

explanation.surface: Someone putting money in, a person with a particular interest in a commercial hub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'business centre' suggests a city district, but 'centre' takes the middle two letters of 'business' and 'involving' wraps the word for an enthusiast round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who manages large sums of money and backs ventures puts capital into them, as an investor does.

clue.text: Bird left vessel in the Flood

parts.note: Noah built the ark to survive the Flood in Genesis

explanation.surface: A bird stayed behind on Noah's boat during the deluge.
explanation.definitionFit: The skylark is a songbird.

clue.text: Caretaker, perhaps, injured in a gun raid

indicators.note: something injured is damaged, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A building's caretaker was hurt in an armed attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injured' rearranges A GUN RAID. 'perhaps' shows the definition is an example: a caretaker is one kind of protector.
explanation.definitionFit: A caretaker looks after property, one example of a keeper or protector.

clue.text: Presumably anti-Royalist battle?

parts.note: agin is a dialect form of against, so it means anti
the Court party were the supporters of the monarch, the royal court

explanation.surface: Asks whether a historic battle was fought by opponents of the crown.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated 'anti-Royalist' splits into dialect for against and the king's party, so the battle of 1415 reads as 'against the court'; the question mark flags this playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry V of England defeated the French in the battle of 1415 at this place in northern France.

clue.text: Person who has depressing experience needs day off at the outset

indicators.note: the abbreviation for day is taken off from the start of the word, which is where the outset is

parts.note: a downer is something that makes you feel low

explanation.surface: Someone going through a bleak time needs a day off first thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who possesses a thing is its proprietor, the holder of it.

clue.text: Medal, one secured by big shots being very successful

indicators.note: the letter for one is held secure inside the word for medal

parts.note: gong is British slang for a medal or decoration
I is the Roman numeral one
great guns are important people, as are big shots

explanation.surface: A decorated soldier, one guarded by heavy artillery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big shots' looks like weapons in the surface, but it means important people, great guns. GONG is British slang for a medal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means doing extremely well or making rapid progress.

clue.text: Stress, as one may describe teenage years?

definitions.meaning: to emphasise something, as by drawing a line beneath it

definitions.text: as one may describe teenage years?
definitions.meaning: the teens are the ages below twenty, a score being twenty

explanation.walkthrough: A score is twenty, so the teenage years fall short of a score.
explanation.definitionFit: To emphasise is to put a line beneath; and teens fall below a score, twenty years.

clue.text: I half-heartedly cut and ran?

indicators.note: the word for cut has a double letter at its heart, and only half of that pair is kept

parts.note: to lop a branch is to cut it off, so lopped means cut

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to slashing at something without real commitment and then fleeing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' drops one of the two Ps at the centre of LOPPED. The 'I' casts the clue as the speaker's confession.
explanation.definitionFit: To lope is to run with long easy strides, so the past tense means ran.

clue.text: TV show is on, up to start of shipping forecast

parts.note: prog is short for programme, a TV show

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the words is and on are read from the bottom, in reverse
start of means the first letter of shipping is used

explanation.surface: A television programme is on, leading into the shipping forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns IS ON into NOSI; 'start of' gives S from 'shipping'. The shipping forecast is a long-running British radio weather bulletin for sea areas.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's prediction of how an illness will go is a forecast of its course.

clue.text: Purpose in announcing strained relationship

indicators.note: announcing means the phrase is said out loud and heard as another word

parts.note: a strained relationship is one held in tension, a state of strain between people

explanation.surface: Wonders about the reason for broadcasting news of a difficult relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link here; spoken, 'in tension' sounds exactly like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aim or plan is what one means to do, which is a purpose.

clue.text: Making intense efforts, not having succeeded in practice

indicators.note: not having means the letter for succeeded is taken away

parts.note: straining means trying very hard
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in family trees and lists of rulers

explanation.surface: Trying very hard but failing to win while rehearsing.
explanation.walkthrough: S for 'succeeded' comes from genealogies and lists of monarchs.
explanation.definitionFit: Practice and drills to build skill make up a course of preparation.

clue.text: A wind soon blows up in this mountainous region

indicators.note: a wind blowing up scatters things, so the letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: A gale will soon rise in this hilly area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blows up' rearranges A WIND SOON. The region is a national park in north Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The national park around the highest peak in Wales is a region of mountains.

clue.text: Decline a delivery

definitions.meaning: a fall in number or amount, as in a fall-off in sales
the act of leaving goods or a passenger at a place

explanation.definitionFit: A falling-away in numbers is a decline; leaving a parcel or passenger somewhere is a delivery.

clue.text: Extract from letters, extremely brief

indicators.note: Extract from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A passage taken from some very short correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse and brief both describe speech or writing using few words.

clue.text: Girl upset as before after this is mislaid

indicators.note: after places the anagram after the shortened word
is mislaid means the letters i and s are lost from the word this
upset means knocked over, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A young woman is distressed as before because this has been lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges AS and ERE (old word for before) into ERESA; 'after' puts that behind what remains of 'this' once 'is mislaid' removes its I and S.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a female first name, so it names a girl.

clue.text: Troubles among ladies and gents?

parts.note: in means among, as in 'in the crowd'
conveniences is a British euphemism for public toilets, signed Ladies and Gents

explanation.surface: Problems arising in public toilets.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain public toilets are signed Ladies and Gents and politely called public conveniences.
explanation.definitionFit: Annoyances or nuisances are troubles, and the plural noun fits the plural definition.

clue.text: Serviceman put bomb on transport

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: the V1 was a German flying bomb of the Second World War, written with Roman numeral one
a car is a means of transport

explanation.surface: A soldier planted a bomb on a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serviceman' suggests the armed forces, but a vicar is one who conducts church services. The V1 bomb is written VI.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish priest takes church services, so he is a man of services in a punning sense.

clue.text: Sound ringing 1 ac

definitions.meaning: the short sharp noise of glasses touched together
the answer to 1 across, in its slang sense of prison

explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 1 across is also slang for prison, and so is this word.
explanation.definitionFit: A clinking noise is a light ringing sound; both this and the 1 across answer are slang for jail.

clue.text: Wound caused by shot in the dark?

definitions.meaning: a cut made with a knife or dagger
a wild guess, an attempt made without knowing

explanation.surface: An injury inflicted by someone firing blindly at night.
explanation.definitionFit: A knife puncture is a wound; making a guess is having a go at something blindly.

clue.text: Poet relaxed efforts? No good abandoning rhymed work

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Poet relaxed efforts? No good abandoning rhymed work (5)' for TASSO: SONG less NG (no good) could give SO, but no sense of 'relaxed efforts' gives TAS, and no source found settles the parse; possibly an OCR misreading.
annotationWithheld.clue: Poet relaxed efforts? No good abandoning rhymed work

clue.text: Set income, terribly small amount in some countries

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly damaged, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A fixed income that turns out to be a pitifully small sum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges SET INCOME. The answer is the hundredth part of a currency unit in Italy formerly and in some Latin American countries.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a coin worth one hundredth of a lira, peso or similar unit, so a tiny sum in those places.

clue.text: Vehicle rental firm's first to be engulfed in wild flames

parts.note: a bus is a road vehicle

indicators.note: to be engulfed means to be swallowed up inside the word for rental

parts.note: hire is the British word for renting something

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the word firm's is used

explanation.surface: A coach-hire company's premises are the first to go up in flames.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' gives F, the opening letter of 'firm's', and 'to be engulfed' puts it inside HIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire raging through scrub or forest is a wildfire, uncontrolled flames.

clue.text: Confront two animals on the way back

indicators.note: on the way back means the two animal words are read in reverse

parts.note: an elk is a large deer
a cat is a common pet animal

explanation.surface: Two creatures met on the return journey.
explanation.walkthrough: ELK and CAT together read backwards make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To tackle a problem or person is to face it head on.
